children: Costa Rica's central bank bought nearly 85% of the dollars traded on the country's foreign exchange platform on November 13 as the US currency fell to an all-time low against the colón,

The Banco Central de Costa Rica (BCCR) has bought foreign currency steadily this year. It has acquired $1.39bn through stabilisation operations in 2026 and has recorded no sales through that mechanism. The latest purchases came as the weighted average dollar price on the Monex market dropped to $1.00 (CRC446.10). That was $0.0016 (CRC0.72) below the previous session and $0.0016 (CRC0.70) below the record set in September.

The BCCR took $41.8mn of the $49.3mn that changed hands on Monex during the session, a share of 84.8%, according to the bank's intervention records and the market's trading summary. Stabilisation buying accounted for $32.3mn. The remaining $9.5mn covered foreign currency needs of the non-bank public sector.
The $32.3mn stabilisation purchase was the largest single-day intervention of its kind so far in November. It lifted the month's stabilisation total to $127.2mn, up from $94.9mn as of November 12.

Most of that buying was concentrated in four sessions from November 10 onwards, during which the bank picked up $102.6mn in total. It bought $27mn on November 10, $29.6mn on November 11 and $13.7mn on November 12.

Stabilisation interventions are meant to dampen sharp swings in the exchange rate. Public sector operations serve the state's foreign currency requirements. The bank also sold $9.7mn on November 13 to meet public sector needs, a figure separate from the $9.5mn it bought on Monex and excluded from stabilisation totals.

Retail rates published by the BCCR and checked at 3:45pm showed the three state-owned banks selling dollars at between $1.01 (CRC452) and $1.02 (CRC453). Banco de Costa Rica and Banco Popular quoted $0.98 (CRC438) to buy and $1.01 (CRC452) to sell, while Banco Nacional offered $0.99 (CRC439) and $1.02 (CRC453). Among private lenders, BAC matched Banco Nacional, Banco Cathay quoted $0.99 (CRC440) and $1.02 (CRC452.50), and Banco BCT posted $0.98 (CRC436) and $1.02 (CRC454).

title: Costa Rica central bank buys dollars as colón hits record
